tools.hearing-test.faqs.0.question: How should I take this test?
tools.hearing-test.faqs.0.answer: Use headphones in a quiet room, and keep the volume comfortable — never too loud. Play each frequency and honestly mark what you hear.
tools.hearing-test.faqs.1.question: Is this a medical hearing test?
tools.hearing-test.faqs.1.answer: No. It is a quick self-check of your audible frequency range. Please see an audiologist for a professional evaluation.

tools.height-predict.metadata.descriptio: Free online height predictor. Enter the parents' heights and gender of the child to get a rough adult height estimate. Runs in your browser.
tools.height-predict.title: Height Predictor
tools.height-predict.description: Enter the father's and mother's heights and the child's gender to estimate the child's adult height using a common prediction formula.
tools.height-predict.faqs.0.question: How accurate is this?
tools.height-predict.faqs.0.answer: It uses the mid-parental height formula, which is an estimate. Actual height depends on genetics, nutrition and health.
tools.height-predict.faqs.1.question: Is this medical advice?
tools.height-predict.faqs.1.answer: No, it is an educational estimate. Consult a pediatrician for growth concerns.

tools.keycode.faqs.0.question: What is the difference between key and code?
tools.keycode.faqs.0.answer: key is the character produced (e.g. "a" or "A"), while code is the physical key location (e.g. "KeyA"), independent of layout.
tools.keycode.faqs.1.question: Do I need to install anything?

tools.monte-carlo-pi.metadata.title: Monte Carlo Pi - Estimate π with Random Points
tools.monte-carlo-pi.metadata.descriptio: Estimate pi by throwing random points into a circle and counting how many land inside the quarter circle. A fun visual demo. Runs in your browser.
tools.monte-carlo-pi.title: Monte Carlo Pi
tools.monte-carlo-pi.description: Drop random points into a square and count how many fall inside the quarter circle. The ratio approximates π/4, so the estimate converges to π.
tools.monte-carlo-pi.faqs.0.question: Why does this work?
tools.monte-carlo-pi.faqs.0.answer: The quarter circle covers π/4 of the square. With enough random points, the fraction inside the circle approaches π/4, giving an estimate of π.
tools.monte-carlo-pi.faqs.1.question: How accurate is it?
tools.monte-carlo-pi.faqs.1.answer: Accuracy grows with the number of points. With 200,000 points you typically get π correct to about 2-3 decimal places.

tools.online-clock.faqs.0.question: Why are Unix timestamps useful?
tools.online-clock.faqs.0.answer: Unix timestamps are the number of seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC, used in APIs, databases and scripts for unambiguous time values.
tools.online-clock.faqs.1.question: Is the displayed time my local time?
tools.online-clock.faqs.1.answer: Yes — the clock shows your device's local time and updates every second.

tools.pi-digits.faqs.0.answer: A BigInt spigot algorithm computes the digits on the fly in your browser — no server or database is involved.
